@graph.name: Laccase mediator systems do not detectably degrade PFOA or PFOS; the reported loss is sorption to the enzyme
@graph.description: Can a laccase mediator system be optimised to degrade perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), as two earlier reports of modest losses suggested?
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: A statistically significant decrease in PFOA or PFOS mass, not only aqueous concentration, relative to untreated and enzyme-only controls, under conditions where the same enzyme and mediator transform a surrogate substrate.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.system: laccase mediator systems with nitroxyl (N-OH or N-oxyl) mediators in aerated batch reactors at 30 °C
nrr:applicabilityConditions.enzymes: Trametes versicolor laccase (MilliporeSigma) for the TvL experiments; Agaricus bisporus and a native white-rot laccase in the screen; the Pleurotus ostreatus laccase of the prior reports was not available
nrr:applicabilityConditions.substrateConcentrations: 1 uM (screen and two-week experiment) and 0.1 uM (96 h and 24 h experiments)
nrr:applicabilityConditions.matrices: 10 mM CuSO4 pH 5 or 50 mM sodium malonate pH 4.5
nrr:applicabilityConditions.duration: 24 h to 28 days with repeated enzyme and mediator dosing
nrr:applicabilityConditions.analysis: LC-MS/MS, Agilent Triple Quad 6460A, negative electrospray, multiple reaction monitoring; isotope dilution with mass-labelled 13C PFAAs at 2 to 5 ug/L; calibration range 0.2 to 10 ug/L; samples diluted to a target of 10 ug/L; delay column after the purge valve; mobile-phase blanks every 10 samples (Text S2)
nrr:applicabilityConditions.note: the negative is about detectable degradation under these conditions; sorption to the enzyme is shown to mimic up to about 60 % apparent removal when only the aqueous phase is sampled

nrr:invalidators: a mass-balanced demonstration of PFOA or PFOS transformation products by any laccase mediator system
a Pleurotus ostreatus laccase preparation shown to degrade PFAAs with vessel and protein extraction accounted for

nrr:untriedBranches.description: Use rigorous controls, in particular full mass balances including vessel and protein extraction, when evaluating bioinspired PFAS treatments.
Study PFAS-protein binding mechanisms as a route to bioinspired adsorptive materials, noting that the quantity of enzyme needed for adsorptive removal may be prohibitive.
Repeat the prior reports' conditions with a Pleurotus ostreatus laccase, with full mass balance, if a source of that enzyme can be found.

nrr:openQuestions: Why did the earlier Pleurotus ostreatus laccase systems report PFOA and PFOS loss: sorption of the kind shown here, a property of that enzyme, or something else?
Which side chains of TvL bind PFOA after oxidation by the mediator?

nrr:cost.note: batch reactors in triplicate; the longest experiment 28 days; no monetary cost reported

nrr:provenanceNotes: The positive control is a surrogate substrate (carbamazepine) run in a separate reactor set with the same enzyme, mediator and buffer, not an arm of the PFAA experiments. The ingest counts it as a designated positive control for the TvL/HBT findings and says so in each control's note; it does not count for the mediator screen, which used two other laccases.
The ingest treats the stated quantification range and the stated expected effect size as the sensitivity statement; the article reports no formal power analysis.

SI Tables S2 and S3 are images in the PDF; every cell was transcribed into curated/laccase/mass_balance.csv with the row and column as locator. The main text rounds them (82 % recovered becomes '18 +/- 2 % apparent loss').
The article has no author-contribution statement; every author is recorded with the role 'writing' only.
TvL/HBT against PFOS was tested only in the 0.1 uM 96 h and 24 h experiments; the two-week dosing experiment was PFOA only.

nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: The article makes no statement about the use of AI tools.

nrr:confidence.basis: surrogate-substrate positive control passed, radical formation confirmed by EPR, enzyme activity confirmed, triplicate reactors, and a full mass balance including vessel and protein extraction that accounts for the apparent loss

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: While unable to replicate the oxidation of PFAAs, we show that interactions of the PFAA compounds with laccase and laccase mediator mixtures could cause an artifact that mimics transformation (<=60 %) of PFAAs. the LMS appears to be unable to detectably degrade the perfluorinated compounds PFOA and PFOS ... it is particularly important for researchers to use rigorous controls when analyzing treatment and removal strategies with novel bioinspired technologies
@graph.nrr:hypothesis: Improve the scope and efficacy of laccase mediator system (LMS) treatment of perfluoroalkyl acids by a mechanistic investigation of each component, starting from literature reports of modest PFOA and PFOS losses over extended periods.
nrr:nextSteps: Use rigorous controls, in particular full mass balances including vessel and protein extraction, when evaluating bioinspired PFAS treatments.
Study PFAS-protein binding mechanisms as a route to bioinspired adsorptive materials, noting that the quantity of enzyme needed for adsorptive removal may be prohibitive.
